rows.before: types.ts did not export a TownResident interface nor declare a townResidents field on SlotParse. The matching step-255 commit wired up the savefile parser and SaveFileInspector to read and render an 8-slot town-residents table at body 0x1E0E0 (stride 0x22F8), but the type declarations that match those reads/renders were never added — leaving the committed repo in a state where tsc --noEmit reports `Module "./types" has no exported member 'TownResident'` and `'townResidents' does not exist in type 'SlotParse'`. The save-file editor UI therefore cannot render the residents panel (TypeScript compile fails before the React tree is ever built), and the player-facing symptom is: the town-residents section is missing from the inspector.
rows.after: Added the missing pieces of the type contract: a `TownResidentState` union (`'populated' | 'vacant' | 'uninitialised'`), a `TownResident` interface (`index`, `bodyOffset`, `state`, `name`, `firstBytesHex`), and a new `townResidents: TownResident[]` field on `SlotParse` with documentation matching savefile_format.md §30. With these types in place, parser.ts's `parseTownResidents` and SaveFileInspector.tsx's residents Section both compile, and the residents panel renders in the editor.
rows.reason: Step-255 was the consolidation + typeahead commit; it incidentally swept in residents-restoration code in parser.ts + SaveFileInspector.tsx but missed the matching types.ts additions. step-256 closes the gap so the build is green again and the residents panel reaches users. Without this fix the editor's TS compile fails and the residents section never renders — directly matching the bug Tyler reported (town residents missing from the editor).

rows.before: Round-trip test harness had no assertions for the new town-residents parse path. step-255 added the residents parser without coverage.
rows.after: Two new assertion blocks. (1) tongari_en.dsv fixture: all 8 slots in both slot A and slot B parse as 'vacant' (slot 0, zero-filled) or 'uninitialised' (slots 1..7, 0xFF) — matching the raw bytes inspected in the test save; the body offsets for the 8 slots match §30's documented values exactly (0x1E0E0, 0x203D8, 0x226D0, 0x249C8, 0x26CC0, 0x28FB8, 0x2B2B0, 0x2D5A8). (2) upload_12.bin corpus save (from the translation repo's notes/save_analysis/raw/): slot 0 decodes as 'populated' with the UTF-16 LE NPC name モコるん (Mokorun), slot 1 as ラビーな (Rabina), slots 2..3 as 'vacant', slots 4..7 as 'uninitialised'; slot B mirrors slot A. The upload_12 block is gated on the translation repo being present alongside this archive repo and skips cleanly when it isn't, so CI in an isolated checkout still passes the in-repo fixture assertions.
rows.reason: Empirical anchor for the §30 layout. The fixture-only assertions prove the parser handles the 'no residents yet' case the player sees in a fresh save; the upload_12 assertions prove it handles a populated roster (the §30 evidence Tyler's diagnosis brief cites). Without this coverage future refactors could silently re-break residents parsing exactly the way step-262 did when it removed the entire region.

rows.after: Change-tracking entry documenting the types.ts + test additions and the diagnosis of why step-255 left the editor broken for the residents panel.
rows.reason: Required per the project's change-tracking rule (CLAUDE.md §'Change tracking for the public changelog'): every commit must record before/after data so release-time rollup can produce per-version detail pages.

diagnosis_summary.test_save_residents_state: slot 0 = vacant (zeros), slots 1..7 = uninitialised (0xFF); both slot A and slot B mirror this state — Tyler's save has no in-town residents yet, which is the normal state pre-event.
